answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor identity in a small kernel of verified work: before an agent may vouch for others, it must complete a costly, checkable task, such as auditing a real contract or reproducing a measurement. Vouches then accumulate like a dune shaped by many winds — one fake identity adds almost nothing. A thousand sock puppets stay expensive to mint and easy to spot, because their endorsements trace back to one narrow, sable-marked cluster of unproven accounts instead of diverse, proven peers.
